description: LRU cache class with 12 constraints including a banned stdlib shortcut and thread safety.

input.message:
Write a Python class `LRUCache` implementing a least-recently-used cache.
Requirements — ALL must hold:
1. Class named exactly `LRUCache`.
2. Constructor takes `capacity: int`; raise `ValueError` if capacity < 1.
3. Do NOT use `functools.lru_cache` — implement the eviction yourself.
4. `get(key)` returns the value or `None` if absent, and marks the key most-recently-used.
5. `put(key, value)` inserts or updates; updating an existing key must also mark it most-recently-used.
6. When capacity is exceeded, evict the LEAST recently used entry.
7. Both `get` and `put` must be O(1) — use `collections.OrderedDict` (or a dict + doubly linked list).
8. Implement `__len__`.
9. Guard all mutations with a `threading.Lock` so the cache is thread-safe.
10. Full type hints on every method signature.
11. A class docstring, and a comment stating the O(1) complexity.
12. Standard library only.
Output one Python code block and nothing else.
